_comment: Template. The real dat/config.json holds the CouchDB password, is mode
0600, and is never versioned. Recover the password from KeePass.
CRITICAL: customChunkSize, minimumChunkSize and chunkSplitterVersion MUST
match the Obsidian LiveSync plugin's settings on every device. Chunk IDs
are derived from content AND chunk boundaries, so a mismatch makes the
bridge and the plugin write two complete, non-deduplicating chunk sets for
the same files. Symptom: the database grows by tens of thousands of chunks
with zero new file documents, roughly tripling in size each time a client
Encryption is OFF deliberately. With E2EE enabled the same vault produced
a 2730MB database; unencrypted it is 1366MB for identical content, because
encrypted chunks cannot be deduplicated and must be decrypted individually
during reassembly. The plaintext vault already sits beside CouchDB in
/srv/sync/blackvault and the passphrase would live on the same host, so
E2EE protected only against leaked CouchDB credentials without filesystem
access. Turn it back on if CouchDB ever leaves this hardware.
includeInternal is a DOWNLOAD filter only. The bridge can materialise
hidden files that a plugin uploaded, but it can never upload them itself.
Plugins therefore reach the phone via the Mac, not via the bridge.
